### The Beginning of the End for Judah
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/beginning-of-end-for-judah
Passage: 2 Kings 24:1
Points:
- Following Josiah's death, Judah rapidly deteriorated under kings who practiced wickedness.
- Jehoiakim became a vassal to Nebuchadnezzar before rebelling after three years, deepening Judah's crisis.
- The subsequent raids and Babylonian invasion fulfilled prophetic warnings of divine discipline.
- God's execution of promised judgment proves His righteous justice and trustworthiness.
- Believers can take comfort knowing that the Lord's word never fails and He keeps all His promises.

### Read the Bible: 2 Kings 24, Hebrew 6, Joel 3, and Psalm 143
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/2-kings-24-hebrew-6-joel-3-psalm-143/
Passage: 2 Kings 24:3-4
Points:
- Jehoiakim led Judah into spiritual perversion, revived pagan cults, and fostered widespread violence.
- After becoming a Babylonian vassal, Jehoiakim rebelled, provoking devastating attacks by Nebuchadnezzar's forces.
- The unraveling of Judah was not accidental, but happened explicitly at the command of the Lord.
- Divine judgment fell upon the nation due to accumulated guilt, especially the shedding of innocent blood.
- The resulting catastrophe demonstrated God's righteous anger removing an impenitent people from His presence.
